risk_if_not_implemented: Without Data Replication, data, software and system images cannot be reliably restored within required recovery objectives following a disruption. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Data Loss / Integrity Compromise (R-BC-2), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10).

compensating_control_1.name: Data Backups
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to create recurring backups of data, software and/or system images, as well as verify the integrity of these backups, to ensure the availability of the data to satisfy Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs).
compensating_control_1.justification: Data Backups (BCD-24) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Data Replication (BCD-27) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Redundant Secondary System
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to maintain a failover capability, which is not collocated with the primary Technology Asset, Application and/or Service (TAAS), which can be activated with little-to-no loss of information or disruption to operations.
compensating_control_2.justification: Redundant Secondary System (BCD-21) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Data Replication (BCD-27) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
